title: Engineering Tooling
description: Can build a reproducible workstation and diagnose a stuck process or failing run from the terminal — and can choose which tool would answer a stated workflow question.

levels.name: Foundation
levels.description: Can install a documented toolchain, rebuild git, the language runtime and the editor from their own notes in a new terminal, and run ten distinct shell commands without a GUI — under written guidance.

levels.name: Apprentice
levels.description: Can search an unfamiliar tree from the terminal, produce a map that cites the commands used, and leave a debug log of at least three hypotheses tried in order, including ones that were wrong.

levels.name: Practitioner
levels.description: Can independently turn a reported defect into a failing reproduction, a fix and a regression test as separate commits, using the debugger or a recorded command log rather than guessing.

levels.name: Journeyman
levels.description: Can diagnose a failure whose cause is the environment or the toolchain — a PATH, permission, hung process or a profiled hotspot — and name the inspectable evidence that ruled the application code in or out.

levels.name: Mastery Evidence
levels.description: Can review another apprentice's setup notes or debug log, name a missing reproduction step or a committed secret, and teach which tool to reach for first on a machine they did not set up.
